Investigator: analyst J. Reyes. Reviewed by: (blank). Scope: 2026-01-01 to 2026-03-31 activity following alert TM-2026-02210 (many-to-one inbound). Findings: 22 inbound ACH/wire credits from 19 distinct individuals with no apparent commercial tie to the customer, totaling $214,700 (Jan 6 - Mar 24); funds consolidated and forwarded within 24-72 hours in 6 outbound international wires totaling $208,000 to one overseas beneficiary, Calderon Freight Agentes SA; customer contacted 2026-03-30 and stated the inbound funds are 'advance payments from wholesale buyers', providing no invoices, contracts, bills of lading, or customs records; business registered as import/export wholesale, opened 2025-11, expected monthly throughput $40,000. Exhibit log: E1 alert narrative; E2 90-day transaction export; E3 customer call memo (2026-03-30); E4 counterparty screening result: beneficiary Calderon Freight Agentes SA returned a positive match against the institution's internal known-scam-beneficiary list (entry KSB-0091, added 2025-12), noted 'for reference'; E5 business registration extract. Disposition rationale: 'Inbound volume is high but consistent with a new wholesale import business ramping up; customer provided a plausible business explanation; no confirmed illicit source identified. Recommend CLOSE - no further action; continue monitoring.' Escalation decisions: none; no SAR referral made. Timeline: alert 2026-02-14, work started 2026-03-27, closed 2026-04-02. Narrative: a three-paragraph write-up restating the above and concluding the activity is 'unusual but explained', closing the case.

standard the file is held to

Harborview Investigations QA Standard v4 (generic): every closed case must (a) document the source of inbound funds or state it is unverified; (b) resolve any positive counterparty screening match in the disposition rationale or record a documented decision not to escalate; (c) address whether a SAR referral is warranted where a funnel or rapid-movement pattern is present with no verified economic purpose; and (d) contain a dated escalation record. Under section 6.2, a positive match against the known-scam-beneficiary list is a mandatory-escalation trigger.

typology-detection-mapping.md.scenario: An analyst maps the funnel-account typology into monitoring rules for a multi-state money-services business that can see transactions and KYC but no device data.
fills: funnel accounts
Funnel accounts (domestic funnel-account laundering - many geographically dispersed cash or small deposits into one account, rapidly consolidated and then withdrawn or wired out elsewhere).
the institution type and products

A licensed money-services business offering money remittance and check cashing across about 40 retail agent locations in multiple states; customers are retail and small-business; the products are cash-in remittance send/receive and prepaid load.
what fields the monitoring system can actually see

The monitoring system sees transaction records (amount, date/time, direction, channel, agent-location ID, and sending/receiving city-state), KYC and customer profile (name, date of birth, address, ID type, expected use), and the counterparty name where captured on the send. It does not see device fingerprints, IP or login data, or on-chain data.
